text:
sara: Heads-up — when bringing up hf/bert-reranker-v2 via the redwood converter, our reranker MRR dropped ~6% on the devset. Suspect tokenization/pooling mismatch, not model weights. :thinking_face:

mohit: Ugh. Did you compare token counts / special tokens between HF tokenizer and the converted tokenizer?

sara: Yep. Quick diff showed HF tokenizer has `cls_token='[CLS]'` and `sep_token='[SEP]'`, converter was mapping to "<s>" / "</s>" and also set `truncation_side: 'left'` in the converted config. HF training used right-side truncation.

alicia: Left vs right truncation can absolutely shift which tokens the CLS or pooling sees for short contexts. Were you using CLS pooling or mean pooling for embeddings/reranker?

sara: CLS pooling (we relied on the pooler output during training). But the converted runtime uses an internal "CLS fallback" that sometimes returns token 0 embedding when special token mapping differs.

june: Can you paste the tokenizer config you saw? also paste a short example of tokenized ids so we can compare.

sara: Paste below (converted vs HF):

```
# HF tokenizer (from transformers)
{'bos_token': None, 'eos_token': None, 'cls_token': '[CLS]', 'sep_token': '[SEP]', 'pad_token': '[PAD]', 'add_prefix_space': False, 'truncation_side': 'right'}
# converted (redwood)
{'bos_token': '<s>', 'eos_token': '</s>', 'cls_token': '<s>', 'sep_token': '</s>', 'pad_token': '<pad>', 'add_prefix_space': True, 'truncation_side': 'left'}
```

mohit: Oh neat — add_prefix_space toggled to True will change tokenization on leading whitespace. That alone can change subword splits for short queries.

alicia: Also the cls_token changed. If your reranker trained on [CLS] at position 0 but converter replaces with <s> which the runtime treats differently (like a segment marker), pooling could be skewed.

june: Did you check snippet tokenization for a query example?

sara: Example: `query = "who wrote the catcher in the rye"`
HF: `tokenizer.encode(query) -> [101, 2040, 3115, ... , 102]`  (CLS=101, SEP=102)
converted: `-> [0, 1543, 5312, ... , 2]`  (CLS=0, SEP=2)

mohit: CLS=0 is suspicious — could be being treated as padding in some parts of the pipeline. If the runtime zeroes out pad token vectors, then your CLS vector becomes zeros.

sara: Exactly. We see near-zero vectors for a subset of requests in logs. Explains MRR hit.

alicia: Quick mitigation: set pooler to "mean" over non-pad tokens for the reranker or explicitly set `cls_token` to '[CLS]' in converter mapping and ensure `pad_token_id != cls_token_id` and truncation_side='right'. Also ensure `add_prefix_space` matches HF.

mohit: For a/longer term, add a conversion test in the onboarding pipeline that runs tokenization equivalence checks: sample 1000 dev queries, verify token ids + counts and token-to-text roundtrip nearly identical. Fail conversion if >1% mismatch.

sara: I'll add a quick hotfix to the model config to force `truncation_side: 'right'` and `cls_token: '[CLS]'` and re-run eval. If that fixes it, we can push a conversion-hook change.

build-bot: conversion-job-38721 finished: model artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-models/bert-reranker-v2/1769993344/ :white_check_mark:

june: Also flag for quantization note — when we did int8 experiments on this family, we saw minor rank ordering changes. If converter also changes tokenizer, small quantization noise can amplify. Run quantized evaluation separately.

sara: Good point. I'll run float32 + int8 evals after the tokenizer fix. Planning: (1) force tokens/truncation to HF defaults, (2) re-eval float, (3) run int8 and compare MRR, (4) add tokenization equivalence test to onboarding.

alicia: Thanks — ping if you want help with the conversion hook. Also consider adding an explicit mapping for chat templates: when converting models used as chat templates, many HF chat wrappers add role tags which can insert extra tokens and shift positions.

sara: Will do. Posting quick checklist in case someone needs to reproduce: 
- dump `tokenizer.config.json` from HF and converted artifact
- compare `add_prefix_space`, `truncation_side`, `special_tokens_map` and token ids for CLS/SEP/PAD
- run sample tokenization diffs (5k queries) and surface distribution of differences
- verify pooling code treats cls_token_id != pad_token_id and doesn't zero cls embedding

mohit: Nice checklist. If you want I can add a small script to the repo that fails CI if any of the 4 key fields differ.

sara: Please. That would save a future regression. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
